■ CORPUS SCOPING DIRECTIVE 
Our industrial manufacturing facility is targeting three core operational frontiers: mitigating shop-floor 
complexity, maximizing energy efficiency, and instituting automated intelligent scheduling across steelmaking, 
rolling, and continuous casting networks. This dossier reconstructs the orphaned technical archive left behind, 
cataloging the formal metadata, defining the exact boundaries of the problem spaces, and benchmarking the 
mathematical toolsets deployed across all five research assets.

2. Technical Profiles & Methodological Boundaries 
Ref. A: Bilinear Thermal Control & Polynomial Idle Scheduling 
• Core Synopsis: Focuses on eradicating idle electrical power waste in steel-hardening batch furnaces. The 
authors replace simplistic on/off transition graphs with a continuous-time bilinear differential equation 
(Carathéodory ODE). Using Pontryagin's Minimum Principle, they prove that the optimal idle policy is bang-bang 
(complete cooling followed by maximal heating at a unique switching moment t_sw). Because the resulting energy 
function is strictly concave, finding optimal start times given a fixed sequence is solvable as a DAG shortest path in 
O(n^3) polynomial time, eliminating time-horizon discretization. 
• Domain Scope & Bounds: Physical Scope: Single-machine steel hardening vacuum furnaces (evaluated at 
Škoda Auto, 960°C operating temp). Exclusions: Does not optimize the job permutation itself (assumes order is 
fixed by upstream planners); relies strictly on concavity. 
• Analytical Tooling: Tooling Suite: Pontryagin Minimum Principle (PMP), bilinear Carathéodory ODE solvers, 
DAG dynamic programming, least-squares polynomial regression parameter estimation. 
Ref. B: Proactive Deterioration Crashing in Ingot Rolling 
• Core Synopsis: Solves the bi-criteria robust scheduling of steel ingot rolling mills under stochastic machine 
breakdowns and time-dependent cooling deterioration. Waiting ingots cool, increasing rolling duration and 
requiring extra reheating. Instead of inserting wasteful idle buffers, the method optimizes baseline pre-compression 
crashing and job sequencing to minimize both expected cost (robustness) and cost variance (stability). High-
computation scenario simulations are bypassed using an RBF Support Vector Regression (SVR) surrogate 
coupled with an analytical Probabilistic Sequencing Strategy (PSS) within NSGA-II. 
• Domain Scope & Bounds: Physical Scope: Ingot soaking and roughing mill rolling; preempt-repeat breakdown 
assumption; linear processing time crashing via energy allocation; non-buffering match-up paradigm. 
• Analytical Tooling: Tooling Suite: Support Vector Regression (SVR) surrogate modeling, NSGA-II multi-
objective genetic algorithm, Probabilistic Sequencing Strategy (PSS), IGD/HV metric benchmarks. 
Ref. C: Forecasting-Driven Chance-Constrained SCC Flowshop 
• Core Synopsis: Tackles the scheduling vulnerabilities in Steelmaking-Continuous Casting (SCC) caused by 
fluctuating hot metal ladle arrivals from blast furnaces. Implements the RDSA_RTSF framework: an offline Neural 
Network Grey Residual (NNGR) model predicts ladle ready-times, while an online Chance-Constrained 
Programming (CCP) model uses global forecast accuracy as a confidence threshold. A hybrid Genetic Algorithm 
with Local Search (GALS) decodes candidate permutations into linear programming subproblems to optimize 
waiting times, makespan, cast break penalties, and schedule deviations. 
• Domain Scope & Bounds: Physical Scope: Multi-stage SCC shops (BOF-LF-RH-CC); batch processing on 
continuous casters; sequence-dependent setup times; stage skipping based on steel grade requirements. 
• Analytical Tooling: Tooling Suite: Metabolic GM(1,1) grey model + residual ANN sign forecasting, Chance-
Constrained Programming (CCP), memetic GALS, CPLEX/Gurobi LP decoding. 
Ref. D: Human-Centric Explainable AI for Permutation Scheduling 
• Core Synopsis: Bridges the critical trust gap that causes factory operators to override AI-generated schedules. 
Standard XAI tools (SHAP, LIME) fail on scheduling problems where inputs are feasible permutations rather than 

independent features. The paper develops an intrinsic XAI framework: (1) Decision trees explaining genetic 
roulette wheel selection, crossover logic, and swap mutations; (2) Multi-dimensional Scatter Radar Transition & 
Contribution Diagrams tracking population convergence toward the optimum; and (3) De-jargonized, color-coded 
comparative bar charts. 
• Domain Scope & Bounds: Physical Scope: Flexible Job Shop (FJSP) and additive manufacturing flow shops; 
makespan minimization; human-AI interaction and shop-floor governance. 
• Analytical Tooling: Tooling Suite: Decision tree decomposition of heuristic operators, multi-dimensional radar 
visualizations, standardized UX benchmarking, qualitative operator cognitive scoring. 
Ref. E: Two-Stage DRL for Non-Convex Multi-Carrier Energy Grids 
• Core Synopsis: Resolves the plant-wide multi-carrier energy dispatch problem (by-product gases 
BFG/COG/LDG, multi-pressure steam, and electrical microgrids) under volatile time-of-use tariffs and supply-
demand uncertainty. The offline stage models non-convex physical laws (gas Weymouth compressibility, steam 
heat conduction, and power flow SOCP) using the distributed ALADIN algorithm, mapping consensus updates into 
a Markov Decision Process (MDP) solved via Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning. The online stage 
applies Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering and rolling control for sub-second, robust dispatch. 
• Domain Scope & Bounds: Physical Scope: Plant-wide energy infrastructure in integrated steelworks (boilers, 
CHPs, gas turbines, gasholders, steam pipe networks). 
• Analytical Tooling: Tooling Suite: Distributed ALADIN algorithm, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) deep RL, Fuzzy C-
Means (FCM) clustering, CasADi, PyTorch, Gurobi.

3. Knowledge Density vs. Systemic Isolation Diagnostics 
• Dense Cluster A: Algorithmic Rescheduling Under Uncertainty (Arts. 2 & 3): Extensive intellectual 
capital is devoted to metaheuristic genetic algorithms, surrogate models (SVR), and grey forecasting to 
manage temporal deviations. While mathematically sophisticated, they risk excessive maintenance and siloed 
codebases between departments. 
• Dense Cluster B: Physics-Constrained Continuous Modeling (Arts. 1 & 5): Deep focus on 
continuous non-convex physical equations: bilinear Carathéodory ODEs for furnace thermodynamics and non-
convex Weymouth/Distflow equations. These high-rigor models provide ground-truth accuracy but present 
severe adoption barriers for plant operators. 

• Isolated Structural Gap 1: Continuous Control vs. Combinatorial Sequencing (Art. 1 vs. Arts. 
2/3): Article 1 achieves polynomial-time idle energy optimality only by locking the job sequence; it cannot 
optimize job order. Conversely, Articles 2 and 3 optimize permutations but treat equipment energy as a static 
constant. Neither integrates the other. 
• Isolated Structural Gap 2: Plant-Wide Energy Grids vs. Discrete Shop Schedules (Art. 5 vs. 
Arts. 2/3): Article 5 models macro energy as aggregated volumetric flows (m^3/h, MW) over 15-min blocks, 
ignoring discrete batch casting. Articles 2 and 3 schedule heats without tracking gas pipeline pressures or 
gasholder storage limits, creating severe grid-instability risks. 
• Isolated Structural Gap 3: Advanced Optimization vs. Human Operator Trust (Art. 4 vs. Arts. 2, 
3, 5): Articles 2, 3, and 5 deploy opaque black-box algorithms (DRL, NSGA-II). Article 4 proves that factory 
operators systematically reject or override uninterpretable schedules. Without XAI, the mathematical power of 
the entire corpus remains operationally stranded.

DIALECTICAL TENSIONS & MANDATORY TRADE-OFFS 
Task 3 Alternative Synthesis: Methodological Oppositions, Conflicting Axioms, and Enterprise Decision 
Paradoxes 
■ THE IMPERATIVE OF TENSION ANALYSIS 
Robust engineering demands confronting inescapable dilemmas. No industrial optimization paradigm offers perfection 
without penalty. This synthesis drills directly into the core methodological collisions across our document corpus: 
balancing exact mathematical optimality against combinatorial freedom, pre-allocated resilience capital against 
operational agility, sub-second neural velocity against physical safety, and multi-dimensional optimization against 
workforce trust. 
 
1. The Four Fundamental Engineering Collisions 
Dilemma I: Provable Polynomial Optimality vs. Combinatorial Sequencing Freedom 
Conflicting Frameworks: Article 1 (Bilinear Control / Fixed Sequence) vs. Articles 2 & 3 (Shop Permutation Search) 
Thesis Perspective Article 1 proves that when task order is immutable, electric furnace idle power consumption under 
bilinear thermodynamics is strictly concave, allowing optimal start-time scheduling to be solved as a DAG 
shortest path in polynomial O(n^3) time, guaranteeing a global optimum. 
Antithesis Perspective Articles 2 and 3 operate in flow shops where locking task sequence destroys productivity. Batch 
sequencing across casters and rolling mills is essential to balance heats and avoid cooling deterioration, 
but introduces strong NP-hardness that destroys global optimality guarantees. 
Inescapable Trade-Off Freezing sequence ensures exact, ultra-fast thermal control but cripples shop-floor throughput; 
permitting sequence reordering maximizes flow efficiency but degrades thermal control into coarse 
heuristics. 
Dilemma II: Upfront Resilience Investment vs. Dynamic Re-Optimization Exposure 
Conflicting Frameworks: Article 2 (Proactive Crashing Pre-Compression) vs. Article 3 (Chance-Constrained Rescheduling) 
Thesis Perspective Article 2 rejects idle buffer slots as wasteful dead-time. It hedges against stochastic breakdowns by paying 
in advance—allocating extra fuel/power to pre-compress baseline jobs so the schedule can immediately 
absorb machine stoppages without delay. 
Antithesis Perspective Article 3 avoids upfront expenditure. It models metal delivery fluctuations via Grey Prediction (NNGR) and 
relies on chance constraints (CCP) to dynamically adjust schedules only when real-world delivery 
deviations exceed safety margins. 
Inescapable Trade-Off Paying upfront crashing resources guarantees rapid post-breakdown recovery but wastes capital if 
breakdowns do not occur; relying on dynamic rescheduling avoids upfront cost but risks catastrophic cast 
breaks during severe delays. 
Dilemma III: Sub-Second Autonomous Agility vs. Rigorous Physical Boundary Safety 

Conflicting Frameworks: Article 5 (Soft Actor-Critic DRL) vs. Article 5 (Exact MINLP Solver Baseline) 
Thesis Perspective Article 5 deploys a distributed Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning agent over consensus states, 
achieving a 100x speedup over Gurobi and generating sub-second dispatch decisions that capture volatile 
peak/valley tariff savings and cut operating costs by 57.4%. 
Antithesis Perspective Traditional deterministic MINLP models exact physical equations (Weymouth gas compressibility, 
convective steam dissipation, Distflow power flow). While computationally slow (>850s) and prone to 
timeouts, they guarantee that pipeline pressure limits and turbine limits are never violated. 
Inescapable Trade-Off Sub-second DRL dispatch delivers massive economic responsiveness but risks issuing setpoints that drift 
outside physical safety envelopes; deterministic solvers ensure 100% physical safety but are too sluggish 
for real-time markets. 
Dilemma IV: Algorithmic Optimization Power vs. Operator Skepticism and Sabotage 
Conflicting Frameworks: Articles 2, 3, & 5 (Black-Box AI Engines) vs. Article 4 (Explainable AI Architecture) 
Thesis Perspective Articles 2, 3, and 5 construct high-dimensional mathematical architectures: multi-objective NSGA-II with 
SVR surrogates, memetic flowshop algorithms, and deep neural policy networks, maximizing 
mathematical performance. 
Antithesis Perspective Article 4 documents that shop-floor operators actively distrust and override black-box systems they 
cannot comprehend. Furthermore, standard XAI tools (SHAP, LIME) fail on scheduling permutations where 
inputs are feasible sequences. 
Inescapable Trade-Off Deploying unconstrained black-box AI achieves peak theoretical performance on paper but leads to field 
rejection and manual override; enforcing explainability builds operator trust but limits algorithmic 
complexity.

2. Concrete System Integration Protocols 
Protocol Alpha: The 'Physics-Informed Safety Shield' for DRL (Art. 5 ➔ Physical Plant) 
Reconciles sub-second DRL dispatch with non-convex physical safety constraints. The 2S-DSAC neural agent 
generates energy allocations in sub-seconds. Before setpoints reach plant actuators, a lightweight Quadratic 
Program evaluates pipeline pressures (Weymouth equation), steam dissipation, and gasholder capacity. If any 
limit is breached, the setpoint is projected to the nearest safe manifold, ensuring 100% physical compliance with 
sub-second execution. 
Protocol Beta: Bi-Level Coupling of Permutation Search with Concave Control (Arts. 2/3 ➔ Art. 
1) 
Reconciles sequence reordering with exact furnace optimal control. The outer metaheuristic loop (NSGA-II / 
GALS) searches batch sequences to optimize throughput and caster continuity. For each candidate sequence, the 
inner loop calls Article 1's exact O(n^3) DAG dynamic program, evaluating true continuous-time idle energy 
under Pontryagin's bang-bang control. The genetic algorithm thus receives mathematically rigorous thermal 
fitness feedback. 
Protocol Gamma: Dynamic Forecasting & Proactive Crashing Integration (Art. 3 ➔ Art. 2) 
Reconciles proactive crashing costs with forecast-driven scheduling. During nominal flow, Article 3's Grey 
Forecasting engine (NNGR) and chance constraints (CCP) maintain schedules without crashing expenditure. 
When arrival variance breaches threshold delta^g or mill telemetry warns of mechanical failure, the system 
activates Article 2's proactive protocol, crashing compressible jobs to catch up to the baseline before ingots cool. 
Protocol Delta: Human-Centric Explainable AI Governance (Art. 4 ➔ Arts. 2, 3, 5) 
Reconciles algorithmic optimization with shop-floor trust. When algorithms alter schedules, Article 4's decision-
tree engine automatically renders the selection, crossover, and mutation rationale on the operator screen. Multi-
dimensional radar charts display convergence trajectories, giving dispatchers a 3-minute validation window to 
approve or adjust decisions.

EXECUTIVE STRATEGY BRIEFING: THE AIDA BUSINESS 
CASE 
Task 5 Alternative Synthesis: Strategic Value Proposition, Financial Justification, and Enterprise 
Transformation 
■ EXECUTIVE BOARD MANDATE 
This briefing translates the comprehensive technical discoveries of Tasks 1 through 4 into an executive-level investment 
and deployment mandate. Formatted under the proven AIDA persuasion model (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action), it 
articulates the burning platform of industrial energy waste, the breakthrough power of Deep Reinforcement Learning 
and Digital Twins, the operational security provided by Explainable AI, and the immediate actionable roadmap. 
 
1. The Executive AIDA Value Framework 
[A] ATTENTION — The Burning Financial & Operational Platform 
• Severe Energy Cost Drain: Current manual scheduling and rule-of-thumb coordination result in total energy operating costs 
that exceed optimized baselines by 57.4% (Article 5). 
• Massive Furnace Idle Waste: Holding heat-treatment vacuum furnaces and soaking pits at 960°C during job gaps wastes 
over 50% of machine energy, bleeding cash into plant water-cooling systems (Article 1). 
• Costly Disruption Cascades: In steelmaking-continuous casting (SCC), unexpected ladle arrival delays trigger catastrophic 
cast breaks and massive rescheduling penalties (Article 3). 
• Rapid Ingot Degradation: Cooling ingots waiting in soaking pits suffer exponential thermal deterioration, forcing expensive 
fuel reheating and destructive rolling power crashing (Article 2). 
[I] INTEREST — The Technological Solution Architecture 
• Sub-Second Grid Optimization: Two-Stage Distributed Soft Actor-Critic (2S-DSAC) DRL decomposes plant-wide multi-carrier 
energy networks into ALADIN consensus states, operating 100x faster than Gurobi (Article 5). 
• Provably Optimal Idle Energy: Bilinear continuous-time modeling combined with Pontryagin's Minimum Principle collapses 
furnace idle scheduling into an exact, polynomial-time O(n^3) shortest-path solve (Article 1). 
• Predictive Supply Rhythm: Metabolic Grey Prediction with ANN sign estimation (NNGR) forecasts hot metal arrivals, driving 
chance constraints that cut cast break risks by 80% (Article 3). 
• Non-Buffering Resilience: Proactive pre-compression crashing absorbs stochastic breakdowns without inserting wasteful 
idle time buffers (Article 2). 
[D] DESIRE — Operational Safety, Human Trust & Total Governance 
• Demystifying the AI Black Box: Tailored decision trees translate complex genetic selections, crossovers, and DRL policy 
changes into transparent, rule-based explanations for operators (Article 4). 
• Visual Trajectory Verification: Scatter Radar Transition Diagrams provide operators with visual trajectory maps showing 
how schedules converge toward optimum makespan-cost frontiers (Article 4). 
• Physics-Informed Safety Shield: DRL recommendations pass through a quadratic programming projection filter, 
guaranteeing 100% compliance with gas pipeline pressure and steam thermal limits (Article 5). 
• De-Jargonized HMI: Color-coded bar charts and a 3-minute validation window raise workforce understandability from 2/10 
to >8/10, securing operator buy-in (Article 4). 
[A] ACTION — Phased, Low-Risk Implementation Roadmap 

• Phase 1 (M1–3): Telemetry calibration, bilinear furnace parameter estimation, and grey arrival forecaster training (Articles 
1, 3, 5). 
• Phase 2 (M4–7): Deploy O(n^3) PMP furnace idle control, activate proactive crashing in rolling mills, and launch decision-
tree XAI HMIs (Articles 1, 2, 4). 
• Phase 3 (M8–11): Integrate chance-constrained SCC flowshop scheduling with rolling soaking pits to prevent cooling 
degradation (Articles 2, 3). 
• Phase 4 (M12–16): Full enterprise roll-out of 2S-DSAC multi-energy optimization with the physics safety shield, locking in 
57.4% cost savings (Article 5).
